features.name: HourlyCertificateRegistry contract (multi-issuer hourly certificates)
features.summary: Operator manages issuers. Issuers register plants and issueBatch hourly kWh certificates (id = generator<<64|hour), once per plant-hour, only by the registering issuer.
features.registry_match: Hourly certificates from several issuers, one shared retirement state

features.name: Shared retirement state across issuers
features.summary: retire() updates a single matched[consumer][hour] counter regardless of which issuer's certificate is used, and is limited to unmatched consumption for that hour.
features.registry_match: Hourly certificates from several issuers, one shared retirement state

features.name: Transfer-once rule
features.summary: transfer() only works from the plant owner account, so a certificate moves at most once from plant to buyer (OnlyOneTransfer). transferBatch is also provided.
features.registry_match: Transfer-once rule and wallet-bound company retirement

features.name: Wallet-bound company retirement, same-hour only
features.summary: The operator binds a company id to one wallet via registerConsumer. Only that wallet can retire or anchor claims, the certificate hour must equal the consumption hour, and retirement cannot exceed unmatched use.
features.registry_match: Transfer-once rule and wallet-bound company retirement

features.name: Operator-written metered consumption with no-regression correction
features.summary: recordConsumption writes hourly kWh and refuses any correction that would fall below what is already matched. The operator stands in for the meter feed.

features.name: Public matchedBps read and anchorClaim
features.summary: matchedBps computes the hourly matched share on-chain. anchorClaim lets a company wallet anchor a claim hash, with the matched share computed by the contract, immutably.

features.name: In-memory JavaScript ledger mirroring the contract
features.summary: A Ledger class with the same rules, error names and integer arithmetic, so the web demo runs without a chain. A test replays the whole demo week through both.

features.name: Demo scenario builder (fictional parties, real Taipower curves)
features.summary: Builds three fictional plants, three fictional companies and contracts from real Taipower generation shapes. Consumption is sized so certificate volume is 103-105% of use, which makes the demo claim true on paper. It includes a double-sale attempt that the ledger refuses.

features.name: Deterministic claim checker (hourly vs volume basis, verdict, rewrite)
features.summary: Validates structured claims, selects the hours, computes the hourly and volume bps with a 0.5-point tolerance, gives SUPPORTED or NOT_SUPPORTED with reasons, and writes a supportable rewrite on the same basis.
features.registry_match: Claim checker and hour-by-hour evaluation against Taipower open data

features.name: RE100 15-year plant-age rule with 15% allowance
features.summary: For RE100 claims, the checker discounts matched or bought kWh from plants older than 15 years beyond 15% of use. Unknown commission years count as old. Exempt procurement types are not modelled.

features.name: Keyword rule parser for typed claim sentences (no AI at runtime)
features.summary: Turns a sentence into claim fields in the browser, erroring on unknown companies, windows that cross midnight, non-full-hour windows and missing percentages instead of guessing.

features.name: LLM claim parser (evaluation-only, off unless dedicated key and live flag)
features.summary: An OpenAI-compatible client to PublicAI using the SEA-LION model. It stays disabled unless HOURMATCH_LLM_LIVE=1 and LLM_API_KEY are set. The web page uses only cached parses of five examples stored in meta.json, with no live AI call.

features.name: Your own data: CSV upload to the same ledger and checker (browser-only)
features.summary: Parses an hourly-use CSV and a certificate CSV with plant and commission year, builds a ledger scenario, and checks claims with nothing uploaded. Sample CSVs are provided.

features.name: Claim checker web page (claim, fields, verdict, stacked-bar SVG chart, daily table)
features.summary: A three-step static page: paste or pick an example claim, edit the parsed fields, and see the verdict, the on-paper vs hour-by-hour share, an SVG chart and a per-day table. It includes a theme toggle.
features.registry_match: Claim checker and hour-by-hour evaluation against Taipower open data

features.name: Printable one-page report (browser print to PDF)
features.summary: Builds a report with the claim, verdict, chart, per-day table, plants and method, then calls window.print().

features.name: Ledger refusals panel (double-sale attempts)
features.summary: Shows the demo week's rejected second sales from the browser ledger.

features.name: Sepolia panel with a live matchedBps read compared against the browser ledger
features.summary: Lists wallets and demo-day transactions including refused ones, shows the anchored claim, and a button that does eth_call matchedBps against public RPCs and compares with the JS ledger.

features.name: Sepolia deploy and demo-day script with six separate wallets
features.summary: Deploys the registry and writes one demo day with operator, two issuers and three company wallets. It generates the demo wallet keys into .env.local, has a gas-price cap, and includes refused-call cases. The operator key comes from the CLIMATECHAIN_TESTNET_PK environment variable.

features.name: Sepolia deployment records (current and archived v1)
features.summary: deployments/sepolia.json holds wallets, tx hashes, gas and block numbers for the demo day. archive/sepolia_v1.json is the superseded single-wallet contract.

features.name: verify_chain.mjs receipt and matchedBps verifier
features.summary: Re-reads every recorded Sepolia receipt and checks status, matchedBps, consumerWallet and isIssuer against deployments/sepolia.json. Optional --write fills in the gas of refused transactions.

features.name: Taipower open-data fetcher (10-minute snapshots to hourly MWh by fuel)
features.summary: Downloads kiang/taipower_data archive snapshots, aggregates per-fuel subtotals by hour and writes data/taipower_hourly_*.json. Two weekly datasets (2026-09-22 and 2026-10-06) are included.
features.registry_match: Claim checker and hour-by-hour evaluation against Taipower open data

features.name: build_web.mjs static bundle builder
features.summary: Copies the engine modules, the week data, generated sample CSVs, cached parses and eval summaries, and Sepolia selectors/deployment into public/lib, so the demo runs fully client-side.

features.name: Evaluation: HourSync vs LLM-alone vs spreadsheet, dev and holdout weeks
features.summary: run_eval.mjs instantiates 18 dev and 8 holdout claims and scores the system, the pure-LLM and the spreadsheet baseline. There is also an independent Python hand calculation, an xlsx generator, a summarizer, stored results, and RESULTS/SPEND/SPREADSHEET/HANDCALC docs.
features.registry_match: Claim checker and hour-by-hour evaluation against Taipower open data

features.name: Evaluation and hand-calculation section on the page
features.summary: Renders the correct-verdict counts for HourSync, the LLM alone and the spreadsheet on both weeks, with explicit statements of what the evaluation does not show.

features.name: Taiwan T-REC glossary, comparison table and trust-model section
features.summary: A bilingual glossary, a T-REC vs HourSync comparison, an RE100 rule explanation and a 'why a blockchain' panel.

features.name: Test suites (node:test and Hardhat)
features.summary: 26 test cases across 5 files (checker, ruleparse, upload, eval and contract tests). The contract tests cover multi-issuer issuance, one-time issuance, transfer-once, wallet-bound retire/anchor, and a full-week replay equal to the JS ledger.

features.name: README documentation of problem, trust model, gas measurements and Taiwan context
features.summary: Documents the on-chain demo-day table, measured Sepolia gas, the trust model, the T-REC comparison, the checker rules and the evaluation table. It explicitly states all companies and plants are fictional.

limits: Did not verify the live URL or any Sepolia transaction or contract state.
Did not read the full bodies of ruleparse.mjs, upload.mjs, deploy.cjs, fetch_taipower.py, run_eval.mjs or parse.mjs.
No hardcoded secrets found. The deploy script generates wallet keys into .env.local at run time and reads the operator key from an environment variable.
